title: Cellular detection of objectwise weak homotopy equivalences
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed universe. Let $P,Q:\mathrm{sSet}\to\mathrm{sSet}$ be ordinary functors preserving all small colimits and all degreewise injective maps. Let $\eta:P\Rightarrow Q$ be an ordinary natural transformation. Assume $\eta_{\Delta^n}:P(\Delta^n)\to Q(\Delta^n)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every integer $n\geq0$. Then $\eta_X:P(X)\to Q(X)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every small simplicial set $X$, including $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, cellular proof, and Remark 2.2.2.8; weak-homotopy generalization of the same boundary-attachment and filtered-skeleton argument; agent-explicit auxiliary assertion. HTT is read online, archival copy WANTED; no Stacks tag states this assertion.

proof.text: Both $P$ and $Q$ preserve the colimit of the empty diagram. Thus $P(\varnothing)$ and $Q(\varnothing)$ are initial simplicial sets, each isomorphic to $\varnothing$. There is just one map between them, and it is an isomorphism. Its realization has no components or base points, so the weak-homotopy conditions hold. Consequently $\eta_{\varnothing}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, proof, printed p. 77; Remark 2.2.2.8. Generalization to P, Q and eta supplied here.

proof.text: For the finite case, induct first on the bound $d\geq0$ for the dimensions of nondegenerate simplices, and within a fixed $d$ on their number in dimension $d$. The outer base below dimension zero is the empty set: the nondegenerate decomposition implies that a simplicial set without nondegenerate simplices is empty. At the inner base, having no nondegenerate $d$-simplices reduces to the previous dimension bound. Define $\partial\Delta^d$ to be the subobject of maps into $[d]$ which are not surjective; for $d=0$ it is empty. A nondegenerate simplex of $\Delta^d$ is an injective monotone map into $[d]$: a noninjective map factors through a proper surjection, and an injective map cannot be a degeneracy. There are finitely many such injections. In the boundary their dimensions are strictly below $d$. Hence the outer induction gives that $\eta_{\partial\Delta^d}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, also for $d=0$ by Step 1.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, proof, printed p. 77; Remark 2.2.2.8. Generalization to P, Q and eta supplied here.

proof.text: Let $A$ be finite with at least one nondegenerate simplex $\sigma$ of maximal dimension $d$. Apply the top-simplex-removal statement, with this dimension bound and this $\sigma$, to obtain $U\subseteq A$ with one fewer nondegenerate $d$-simplex and no new nondegenerate simplices. Its stated degree conditions are exactly hypotheses (1), (2) and (3) of the simplex-gluing statement, with $n=d$, $V=A$, and $x=\sigma$. That statement therefore gives the pushout $A\cong U\amalg_{\partial\Delta^d}\Delta^d$, using the characteristic map of $\sigma$. The inner induction applies to $U$, giving the weak homotopy equivalence $\eta_U$. The other two comparison maps for this span are $\eta_{\partial\Delta^d}$ from Step 2 and $\eta_{\Delta^d}$ from the hypothesis. The characteristic map need not be an injection, and no such assumption is used.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, proof, printed p. 77; Remark 2.2.2.8. Generalization to P, Q and eta supplied here.

proof.text: Apply $P$ and $Q$ to the pushout in Step 3. Colimit preservation makes both resulting squares pushouts. Naturality of $\eta$ on the boundary inclusion and its attaching map gives a commuting map between the spans $P(\partial\Delta^d)\to P(\Delta^d),P(U)$ and $Q(\partial\Delta^d)\to Q(\Delta^d),Q(U)$. Their three components are weak homotopy equivalences by Step 3. The legs into $P(\Delta^d)$ and $Q(\Delta^d)$ are degreewise injective, since the boundary inclusion is degreewise injective and both functors preserve these maps. Thus the first clause of the gluing statement applies. It says that the induced map on these pushouts is a weak homotopy equivalence. The induced map is $\eta_A$: on each of the two pushout legs this is precisely the naturality equation for $U\to A$ and $\Delta^d\to A$, and maps out of a pushout are uniquely determined by these legs. This completes both inductions and proves the assertion for every simplicial set having finitely many nondegenerate simplices.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, proof, printed p. 77; Remark 2.2.2.8. Generalization to P, Q and eta supplied here.

proof.text: For arbitrary small $X$, let $I$ be its poset of simplicial subsets having finitely many nondegenerate simplices, ordered by inclusion. This is a small set, being a subset of the power set of $\coprod_{n\geq0}X_n$. It contains $\varnothing$. A simplex of a simplicial subset is degenerate in it exactly when it is degenerate in $X$: a degeneracy witness is a face of that simplex and so still lies in the subset. The union of finitely many members therefore again has finitely many nondegenerate simplices; it is an upper bound, including the empty union. Every $x\in X_n$ belongs to such a subset, namely the image of $\Delta^n\to X$, $\alpha\mapsto X(\alpha)(x)$. Indeed factor each monotone $\alpha$ as a surjection followed by an injection. Its image simplex is a degeneracy of the image of that injection; if it is nondegenerate the surjection must be an identity. Thus the nondegenerate simplices of this image belong to the finite list indexed by injective maps into $[n]$. Hence $X=\bigcup_{K\in I}K$. This union is the ordinary degreewise colimit: a compatible family of simplicial maps on the subsets gives one on the union, independent of the subset chosen because two subsets have a common upper bound; it commutes with operators since each subset is simplicial.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.2.7, proof, printed p. 77; Remark 2.2.2.8. Generalization to P, Q and eta supplied here.

proof.text: The restrictions of $P$ and $Q$ to $I$ are small ordinary diagrams. Their colimit cocones $P(K)\to P(X)$ and $Q(K)\to Q(X)$ are colimiting, by Step 5 and preservation of small colimits. Naturality makes the components $\eta_K$ a map of these diagrams. The map it induces on the colimits is $\eta_X$: both maps restrict on each $P(K)$ to $Q(K\hookrightarrow X)\eta_K$, by naturality, and the colimit universal property gives equality. Every $\eta_K$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by Step 4. The poset $I$ is small, nonempty, and every finite subset has an upper bound, as verified in Step 5. The second clause of the gluing-and-filtered-colimit statement therefore proves that $\eta_X$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This applies also to $X=\varnothing$, whose index poset consists of its empty subset.

lean.statement: theorem cellular_weak_homotopy_comparison (P Q : SSet.{u} ⥤ SSet.{u}) [PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} P] [PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} Q] (hPMono : ∀ (A B : SSet.{u}) (f : A ⟶ B), (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective (f.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) → ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective ((P.map f).app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) (hQMono : ∀ (A B : SSet.{u}) (f : A ⟶ B), (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective (f.app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) → ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective ((Q.map f).app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) (η : P ⟶ Q) (hSimplex : ∀ n : ℕ, Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (η.app Δ[n])) (X : SSet.{u}) : Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (η.app X)

Weak equivalence is the recorded SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (realization π0 + based cubical πr), the def-cbc stmt dep's notion; no stronger assumption, no universe restriction; gluing_filtered dep takes I : Type u so proof typable.
